_meta.rule: Every suggestion is at Pending owner decision. Nothing in this directory has been implemented on the strength of its own suggestion. A suggestion is not a plan of work.
_meta.how_to_record: Set decision_status to Approved, Rejected or Deferred and add the date. The page recomputes; nothing has to be edited twice.

suggestions.title: Capture an opening number for every market we originate
suggestions.problem: The price store has an opening number for 272 of 7,239 games, all in 2021, one book, spread and total only. There is no opening moneyline at all. Closing-line value is therefore unmeasurable, and promotion gate P10 with it.
options: Capture one book's opening number each week, by hand, into origin_lab/data/raw/ with a capture timestamp
Buy a licensed historical price feed and backfill
Accept the gap: publish every leaderboard row as struck at the close and say so on the row
suggestions.recommendation: Option 1 as a start. It is the only one that produces a timestamped opening number this season, which is the thing every other option needs.
suggestions.reversibility: Reversible. Nothing downstream changes except that CLV becomes computable.

suggestions.title: Schedule the results feed refresh instead of capturing it once
suggestions.problem: The pinned dataset was two weeks behind the league's own page when this session started. Weeks 8-10 were missing. The feed is right today because it was captured by hand once.
options: Weekly capture from nfl.com, committed with the capture date on every row
Refresh the pinned dataset weekly and re-run the standings reconciliation
Both, official capture as tie-breaker
suggestions.recommendation: Option 3. The reconciliation is cheap and it is the only thing that proves the feed is right.
suggestions.reversibility: Reversible. Rows are appended, never rewritten.

suggestions.title: Decide whether market prices are an admissible correlation input
suggestions.problem: Requirement 7 says official inputs only. Parlay pricing needs a leg correlation, and a leg correlation as usually defined needs a price. The site resolves this by originating its own numbers, but the underlying question is still the owner's.
options: Keep official-only; legs stay defined against our own originated numbers
Admit the pinned market file and fill the four blank rows on correlations.html
Admit it in a separate, clearly labelled tier
suggestions.recommendation: Option 3 if market-dependent numbers are wanted at all. It fills the rows without blurring which numbers are officially sourced.
suggestions.reversibility: Reversible, but it changes what the word 'correlation' means on the site.

suggestions.title: Resolve the player-prop market one way or the other
suggestions.problem: Strategy S8 is a row with no numbers. No official publisher prints prop prices, and no official player-level log is reachable. It has been blocked in three separate builds in this repository.
options: Acquire a licensed prop and player-log feed
Retire the prop market and say so on the site
Keep the schema, revisit when a feed is within budget
suggestions.recommendation: Option 2 or 3. Carrying a permanently blocked row with no decision behind it costs attention that the other seven strategies need.
suggestions.reversibility: Option 3 is reversible; retiring the market is a decision to record, not to reverse lightly.

suggestions.title: Put a capture timestamp on every price snapshot
suggestions.problem: Neither price file carries one. A snapshot with no time is a number of unknown age, and CLV depends on knowing whether a bet was struck before or after the close.
options: Require a timestamp on every write and reject rows without one
Accept date-less numbers and publish the omission on every affected row
suggestions.recommendation: Option 1 for anything captured from now on; option 2 for the historical files, which cannot be back-dated honestly.

suggestions.title: Publish the current week's own lines, with the market comparison
suggestions.problem: The build computes a fair line for all 7,239 games but only shows them where a market number exists to compare against, so the forward book is invisible.
options: Publish forward lines for the next week, with the fair / market / difference columns
Publish them only where a market number exists
Do not publish forward lines from this build
suggestions.recommendation: Option 1, once Q11 is answered. Publishing an own line the owner has not decided the purpose of invites it to be read as a tip.
suggestions.reversibility: Reversible, but a published line cannot be unpublished once someone has acted on it.

suggestions.title: Fund the competition or take the reward language off the site
suggestions.problem: The leaderboard has a scoring rule and a promotion path and nothing to pay with. No strategy has passed promotion, so nothing is eligible either way.
options: Fund a pool and publish the amount
Run it for ranking only
Remove the reward language
suggestions.recommendation: Option 2 until a strategy passes promotion. A reward rule with no money and no eligible strategy is two absences, not a structure.

suggestions.title: Add a decision inbox as the site's front page
suggestions.problem: Choices are scattered across COORDINATION.md, questions.html and suggestions.html. An owner arriving at the site has to read three files to find out what is waiting on them.
options: One page listing every open decision, ranked by what it blocks
A banner on the existing index pointing at the two registers
Leave it as it is
suggestions.recommendation: Option 1. It is the single change most likely to turn the site from an archive into something that gets used.

suggestions.title: Show the verification tier on every table row, not just in the footer
suggestions.problem: A reader has to know whether a row came from the league, from a club, from the pinned dataset or from this repository's own arithmetic. Today that is stated once per page.
options: A small tier badge in the source cell of every row
A colour rule on the row
A per-page legend only
suggestions.recommendation: Option 1. It costs one cell and it removes the single most likely misreading of every table on the site.

suggestions.title: Publish what changed since the last build
suggestions.problem: The repository is worked on by several sessions at once. A returning reader cannot tell which numbers moved, and a moved number that looks unchanged is worse than a wrong one.
options: A changelog page generated from the data file hashes
A 'changed since' marker on rows whose value moved
Nothing
suggestions.recommendation: Option 1. The hashes are already computed; the page is nearly free.

suggestions.title: Decide what the origination model is for, then act on it
suggestions.problem: The model loses to the closing line on all three markets: side MAE 10.59 vs 10.25, total 10.83 vs 10.52, moneyline Brier 0.2208 vs 0.2115. Either that is fine, because the model exists to be an independent baseline, or it is not, because the model exists to beat the market.
options: Keep it as an independent baseline and say so on the page
Replace it and re-run every gate
Keep it and stop leading with the MAE comparison
suggestions.recommendation: Answer Q11 first. This suggestion is downstream of it and should not be started before it.
suggestions.reversibility: Replacing the model is not reversible without re-running everything downstream.

suggestions.title: Settle the club depth-chart tier
suggestions.problem: 31 clubs publish an ordered chart; 12 print 'unofficial' on it. The league publishes none. The depth tables are the only place the site depends on club publications for a numbered fact.
options: Admit club charts as official
Keep them club-published with the disclaimer on every row
Admit only clubs that do not print an 'unofficial' label
suggestions.recommendation: Option 2 until the owner decides. It is the conservative reading and it is already what the site publishes.
suggestions.reversibility: Reversible; the pages reclassify on the next build.
